name: Caiaphas and the council
charge: Seeking false witness against Christ; condemning him by night; delivering him to the Gentiles; forbidding the apostles; stoning Stephen
summary: Caiaphas had already ruled that it was expedient one man die for the people. The council sought false witness to put Jesus to death and found none that agreed; then the high priest adjured him and condemned him for his answer. They delivered him to Pilate, chose Barabbas, and afterward beat and forbade his apostles, and gnashed on Stephen and stoned him.
offense: Every rule of the court broken in one night: witnesses suborned, testimony not agreeing, a capital sentence at night by the accusers themselves, and the prisoner condemned by his own compelled confession. Stephen's charge to them: ye stiffnecked, which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and ye have been now the betrayers and murderers of the Just One.
judgment: Christ told them the kingdom would be taken from them and their house left desolate; Paul says the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost. Peter to their faces: the stone which was set at nought of you builders. Within the generation the temple in which they sat was rubble.

entries.commentary: They accuse him of perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and Pilate says, I find no fault in this man. Matthew's account gives the reason he could see it: he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing. He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

Pilate says a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him. He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Barabbas, cast into prison for sedition and murder, is released, and Jesus is delivered to their will.

Simon a Cyrenian is laid hold upon and made to bear the cross after him. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. If they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Two malefactors, criminals, are led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.

One malefactor railed on him; the other rebuked him, took the blame of his own deeds, and said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. That man repented at the last hour, and was answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

There was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour, and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.
The centurion glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that came together to that sight smote their breasts and returned.

Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man and a just, had not consented to their counsel and deed, and begged the body and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone. He was buried the same day, which is the custom written in the law. There is no waiting days over a body. The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

Peter and John go up to the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour. Counting the way the scripture counts, the day starts at six in the morning: six is the start, so the third hour is nine in the morning, the sixth hour is noon, and the ninth hour is three in the afternoon. Write that down, because knowing how the hours are counted keeps you from being confused later.

A certain man, lame from his mother's womb, is carried and laid daily at the gate called Beautiful to ask alms of those going into the temple. He sees Peter and John about to go in and asks alms, expecting to receive something. This is how you know these are our people, because you primarily see our people begging on the streets, laid low and asking for alms.

Peter says, "Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk." This is why, when people at camp ask if we give money to the poor, we say no. A lot of times we do not know why the Most High put a person in that condition, and the money could end up feeding a drug dealer, a drug addict, or a child molester without our knowing it. The Most High is the one who brings a man low. Sometimes he withholds money, status, or a job to hinder a man from sinning, the way he removed King Manasseh from his power. Many hurtful lusts come from the love of money, and celebrities get caught up in wickedness because riches in the hand of a man who has sin become a tool for evil. He wants to teach you discipline and contentment first, so that when the money comes it is only a tool to pay your bills and support the truth, not to live in the delicacies of this life. -

Peter takes him by the right hand and lifts him up, and immediately his feet and ankle bones receive strength, and he stands, leaps, walks, and enters the temple praising the Most High. Everything the apostles did was prepared and taught to them; they did not move independently. We cannot heal a body today, but we heal every day with the word: drug dealers, baby mothers, and survivors of mental, physical, alcoholic, drug, and religious abuse are healed when they receive the truth. When people say we do not feed the poor, the truth is the poor have the gospel preached to them, and that is the healing. -

All the people see him walking and praising the Most High, know he is the one who sat for alms at the Beautiful gate, and are filled with wonder, running together to Peter and John at the porch called Solomon's. Notice it says "all the people," because a book establishes its characters at the start and then speaks in pronouns, "he," "she," "they," "all," without re-naming the people every time. Christians, and primarily our own people because of a lack of education and reading comprehension, have forgotten who "all the people" are. You have to be war-minded and read into the context so you know the audience, because the verse always clears up who is being addressed, if not in the same verse then in the next. Even in the world, our people who deny the truth get quiet when the scriptures are laid out and the black image of Christ is shown from the Bible, and some wake up on the spot and say, "It is in the Bible, I respect it," which is the spirit of the Most High coming upon them.

When Peter sees it he answers, "Ye men of Israel, why marvel ye at this? or why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?" This is the verse that establishes the audience: the "all the people" of verse 11 are the men of Israel. The healing was not by Peter's own power or holiness. He was not God for doing the work, any more than Elijah was God for raising the dead; it was done by the power of the Most High. This is why the book of Acts is so important, because if you get well versed in Acts you can spiritually kill the white supremacist doctrine and the wicked Christian mindset that has been planted in our people's minds.

Peter names "the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers," who glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up and denied before Pilate when Pilate was determined to let him go. The oath and promise passed through a royal lineage: Abraham had Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, but Ishmael was rejected and Isaac was chosen. If the covenant were for all nations, it would have passed through Ishmael too, but it went straight down to Isaac, showing this is not the God of all nations but the God of our fathers.

They denied the Holy One and the Just and desired a murderer to be granted to them, and killed the Prince of life, whom the Most High raised from the dead, of which the apostles are witnesses. Christians claim the new covenant opened salvation to everybody once Christ died, but the text keeps the promise on the same people.

It is his name, through faith in his name, that made this man strong, and the faith which is by him gave the man this perfect soundness in the presence of them all. The strength did not come from the men but from faith in the name of Christ.

Peter says, "And now, brethren, I wot that through ignorance ye did it, as did also your rulers," but the things the Most High showed before by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he has so fulfilled. Christ fulfilled his suffering; he did not do away with the law and the prophets. If you claim Christ suffered and died for all nations, prove it "by the mouth of all his prophets." Show it through Isaiah, Ezekiel, Jeremiah, or Haggai, that Christ suffered and died for all nations, because the text says all his prophets foretold it. -

"Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord." People say they repented without understanding the scriptural meaning of the words. To repent is to turn from all your transgressions, and to be converted is to change, which requires the law to change to. -

"And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you." The "you" is Israel, which was established back in verse 12, so you have to read the whole chapter as one audience being addressed.

"Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began." Restitution is the restoration of something lost or stolen to its proper owner, the same word used when land seized from our people is demanded back. We are living the restitution of all things right now, before Christ comes. To fit the other nations into this as the gentiles who are grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. The scriptures show the opposite: the nations are the ones who did the stealing and the hiding, so they are not the gentiles being restored. -

"For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things," and every soul that will not hear that prophet shall be destroyed from among the people. The prophet is raised up "from among their brethren," meaning from among men, which proves Christ came through the seed of a man, not immaculate conception. Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept. -

"Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days." All the prophets from Samuel onward foretold these days, tying back to the "you" who are the men of Israel established in verse 12.

"Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations. -

"Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities." "Unto you first" means unto Judah, the Jews first, and the "you" being turned from iniquities is Israel, the same audience throughout the chapter. There was an order and prophecy for the twelve tribes to be redeemed. The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, the "Jews," and the "Jew and Gentile" and "Jew and Greek" language is the split between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom of Israel, not Israel and the nations. The Most High did not cast away the northern tribes; the whole twelve tribes are scattered and being saved. -

As they spake unto the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them, grieved that they taught the people and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead. The Sadducees, Pharisees, elders, and chief priests were the religious leaders of that day, and they are the same religious leaders today: your Creflo Dollars, your TD Jakes, your Joel Osteens, your Gino Jennings, speaking the same things they spoke back then. The Sadducees were the upper class, the wealthy priestly and merchant families, moved by political and economic position. They came under the influence of Hellenism the same way today's pastors come under the influence of Americanism, preaching a prosperity and a political gospel and adopting their own man-made traditions. They were grieved because the teaching pulled the people, the money, and the control away from them. It is jealousy, envy, and the inability to guide the people, the same reason these pastors avoid a real sit-down with someone who actually knows the scriptures. The Sadducees did not even believe in the resurrection, yet they used scriptures they did not believe to try to confound Christ, the same way Christians and five-percenters take our scriptures they reject and use them to try to confound us. -

They laid hands on them and put them in hold unto the next day. The spirit that was on the Pharisees is being activated again, and everyone plays their role again in this lifetime; just as the disciples are back in the truth, the chief priests, Sadducees, and Pharisees are back too, saying the same things they said before. They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched. -

Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed, and the number of the men was about five thousand. Many still hear and believe today, and it is mainly black men leaving the dead churches, because the church gives them no purpose, no structure, no discipline, and no position to lead, teaching them to be docile and subservient. This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law. -

On the morrow the rulers, elders, and scribes, with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, and Alexander, and the kindred of the high priest, gathered together at Jerusalem. Annas had been high priest around 6 to 15 AD and kept the title even after the Romans ejected him, while Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was the official high priest the year Christ was killed. These were the very persons who procured the death of Christ. Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in [Isaiah 53](/bible/isaiah/53) and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim. -

When they had set them in the midst, they asked by what power or by what name have ye done this, and Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, ye rulers of the people and elders of Israel. The conversation is still to Israel, always the Israelites. Being filled with the Holy Ghost did not mean Peter was shaking, sweating, or speaking in tongues; it means he was filled with the wisdom to speak with poise before the rulers. When you are brought before the synagogues, magistrates, and powers, the Holy Ghost teaches you in that same hour what to say, the way brother Abiel spoke eloquently in court and was released. You must be wise as a serpent and harmless as a dove, and the wisdom of God will speak through you. Peter, Paul, John, and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque, or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged, and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors. -

If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole; be it known that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, this man stands here before you whole. Examine our good deeds the same way: taking brothers off the streets from drug dealing, gang banging, killing, and stealing; taking sisters out of prostitution; putting black households back together; keeping children from being aborted; keeping men out of prison. What did the disciples do wrong but heal the impotent man? Any time there is a good deed the Pharisees still attack, which shows the hardness of our people's hearts. It was never about the nation or the people; it was about their own vainglory, position, power, and authority.

This is the stone which was set at naught of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. It was the builders' job to build and bind the nation, to raise up the tabernacle of David, to bind the brokenhearted, and to feed the flock, but when the stone, Christ, came, jealousy and vainglory arose and they rejected him. The kingdom is therefore taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits. Christ is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, because men stumble at his location, his upbringing, his appearance, and his low social class. He came from the same hoods we came from, from your Philadelphias, your Detroits, the south side of Chicago, so the Most High confounds the wise by the foolish and chooses the base and the underdog, the way he chose David, not the Creflo Dollars, the TD Jakes, the Cornel Wests, or the Umar Johnsons who already have a following and would take the glory for themselves. This is how you know God is working with us, taking men called nobody and setting them before princes. Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests. -

Neither is there salvation in any other, for there is none other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved. Christians reduce this to saying the words "in the name of Jesus," but "none other name" means no other power or authority was given to any man; that authority was given to Christ alone, so there is no salvation in Moses or Elias, only through Christ. You cannot sneak into the kingdom through Islam, the Nation of Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormonism, Pentecostalism, Seventh-day Adventism, the Baptists, or Buddhism. Whoever climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber trying to sneak in without laboring; you must enter by the door, which is Christ. -

When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus. The rulers saw these men were not slick, cunning, and crafty like themselves; they were bold, coming as if straight off a plantation and a field, not the regular church men. That boldness is the natural animation of the Holy Spirit, not something you force or make up. Brothers who teach weak, like the Christian pastors, with no power and no conviction, are lacking the Holy Spirit. You cannot push the spirit out; when you keep the Most High's laws and stay in the scriptures, the spirit animates your teaching with boldness, the way Christ taught with authority and not as the scribes. People who call us hostile have simply never seen a man of God speak with the Holy Spirit. Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ. -
Beholding the man which was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it. The living proof of the miracle was standing right there, and the rulers had no answer.

They commanded them to go aside out of the council and conferred, saying what shall we do to these men, for a notable miracle has been done by them and we cannot deny it; but that it spread no further among the people, let us straitly threaten them and command them not to speak in the name of Jesus. It was never about the miracle but about losing their power and their seat of authority, and you have to be that wicked to witness the great works and still plot against the men who did them. Satan cannot cast out Satan, so they knew the miracle was of the Most High; yet the same way they consulted to put Lazarus back to death after Christ raised him, they chose to threaten the disciples rather than glorify God. That level of hatred, envy, and emulation is what the religious leaders had for the people. The Pharisees were divided over Christ, some saying he is not of God because he healed on the Sabbath, others asking how a man that is a sinner could do such miracles. That same division will bring people out of the Christian church to examine the matter and repent based on our works. -

Peter and John answered, whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye, for we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. Having further threatened them, the council let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them because of the people, for all men glorified God for the man who was healed, who was above forty years old.

Being let go, they went to their own company and reported all, and they lifted up their voice to God with one accord: Lord, thou art God who made heaven and earth; why did the heathen rage and the people imagine vain things; the kings of the earth stood up and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. Against the holy child Jesus, Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel were gathered together, and this same thing is going to happen all over again. Their prayer was for boldness to speak the word and that signs and wonders be done, so if you lack the Holy Spirit, your prayer should be that the Most High put it in you, for he gives it freely. When they had prayed, the place was shaken, they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness. -

The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul, and neither said any of them that ought he possessed was his own, but they had all things common. They did not cleave to materialistic things; when you come into the truth those things lose their importance and your objective becomes how you can support the truth. This is the establishment of a community, for community comes from common. With great power the apostles gave witness of the resurrection, and great grace was upon them all; neither was there any that lacked, for as many as owned lands or houses sold them and laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man according as he had need. This was not a prosperity doctrine where you give to get rich; you give so that when one lacks, all supply his need, whether food, an eviction, or a proper burial. The church was the epicenter and hub of the community, and the arms, not tithes, circled through it and were distributed according to each man's need. Joseph, surnamed Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, sold his land and laid the money at the apostles' feet; this is the same Barnabas who later traveled with Paul, and even as an apostle he gave arms. Every ranked man should give arms as a testament of his faith and leadership, even while spending his own money to travel and teach. --- Topics: [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession and kept back part of the price, his wife being privy to it, and brought only a portion and laid it at the apostles' feet. This continues from Acts 4: none among the believers lacked, because those who possessed lands or houses sold them, laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man as he had need. The church was the epicenter of the community, where counsel was given and economic and community problems were resolved, the way the black Wall Street towns like Rosewood and Tulsa once kept the dollar circulating among our own people for months before it left. A community is a people with all things in common: common government, common heritage, common interest, and common culture, and the word community itself comes from the root "common." So-called black people today are not yet a community, divided by religion, politics, and color, until they come into the fullness of Christ. Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry; use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation. -

Peter asks why Satan has filled Ananias' heart to lie to the Holy Ghost and keep back part of the price; while it remained it was his own, so he has not lied unto men but unto the Most High. The spirit upon them was covetousness as well as lying; they saw the full value and coveted it, and did not put away lying as the renewed mind requires. To be renewed in the spirit of the mind is to be born again, to reboot the mind and clear out the programming of this world's philosophy, and to speak every man truth with his neighbour, for we are members one of another. Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform. -

Hearing these words, Ananias fell down and gave up the ghost, and the young men wound him up, carried him out, and buried him. This is after the death of Christ, under grace, yet he was put to death for lying and breaking his vow. Grace was never a licence to sin; the wages of sin is death, even now. The christian church hands out a licence to sin by teaching the law is done away and all is covered by grace, and is answerable for the blood in the community when men sin presumptuously believing there are no consequences. Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure. -

About three hours later Sapphira came in, not knowing what was done, and agreed to the same lie; Peter told her the feet of those who buried her husband were at the door, and she fell down and yielded up the ghost and was buried by him, and great fear came upon all the church. She shared his fate because they agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Most High. A wife is meant to be a tower against death and a help meet; had she refused the evil or brought it to the leadership, she could have saved his life, as Abigail did. A wife submits to her husband as unto the Most High, in righteousness, not in wickedness; if he tells her to break the law, she is not to agree with him. Not everyone has the same measure of grace; one man is put to death for a smaller sin while David was spared far greater ones, for grace is given by the measure of the gift of Christ. The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him. -

By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were wrought; they were together in Solomon's porch, believers were the more added, and multitudes brought the sick into the streets on beds and couches that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow them, and they were healed every one. This is the power poured out after they waited in Jerusalem for the Holy Ghost, fulfilling that these signs would follow them that believe. These gifts of healing and tongues were for that time, to introduce the Son of God and prove the power of the Most High on earth; they are not the gifts of today, which is why our people still die of disease no matter what the pastors claim. In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established. -

The high priest and the sect of the Sadducees, filled with indignation, laid hands on the apostles and put them in the common prison, but the angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night and sent them to stand and speak in the temple all the words of this life. Read the lives of the apostles and prophets as a pattern for today: what the forefathers suffered will come again under America, the last kingdom, and worse; if you teach this gospel, prison and loss will come, so you cannot be joined to this world. Prepare for it: set aside a nest so your wife and family are provided for if you are locked up, for they will freeze accounts and take houses; the Most High will help, but you must still prepare. Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat. -

At dawn the apostles entered the temple and taught; when the council sent to the prison the officers found it shut with all safety and the keepers standing, but no man within, and word came that the men they had imprisoned were standing in the temple teaching the people. This is boldness: freed from prison, they did not hide but went straight back to teach. If they lock you up, go right back out, the way those who truly love their people keep returning no matter how many times they are jailed.

The captain and officers brought them without violence, fearing the people would stone them, and the high priest charged them, saying, did we not straitly command you not to teach in this name, yet you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine and intend to bring this man's blood upon us. It is the same charge leveled today: that teaching the truth fills the cities with this doctrine and tries to lay guilt on the accusers, the way they say teaching history is only meant to make them feel guilty.

Peter and the apostles answer that we ought to obey the Most High rather than men; the God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom they slew and hanged on a tree, and exalted him to be a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. Christ came through the loins of David, from Judah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; the law was given to Israel, so repentance from breaking the law is given to Israel. The apostles are his witnesses of these things because their lineage experienced his ministry, death, and miracles; popes and denominations are not witnesses. The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it. -

Cut to the heart, the council took counsel to slay them, no different from religious leaders today who take counsel against the truth, publish books against it, and would sooner hire accusers than correct themselves. Then Gamaliel, a Pharisee and a doctor of the law held in reputation among all the people, stood up and commanded the apostles to be put outside a little space. When men believe the law is done away they hold no morals to restrain them, and will put the teachers to death thinking they do the will of the Most High. -

Gamaliel warns the council to take heed what they do: before these days Theudas rose up boasting himself to be somebody, and about four hundred joined him, but he was slain and his followers scattered to nothing; after him Judas of Galilee drew people in the days of the taxing and also perished, and his followers were dispersed. The record of Josephus tells the same of Theudas, a magician who persuaded a great part of the people that he was a prophet who could divide the river Jordan, until horsemen fell on them, killed many, and beheaded him; examine such men and see what their work comes to. Therefore refrain from these men and let them alone: if this counsel or work be of men it will come to nought, but if it be of the Most High it cannot be overthrown, lest they be found to fight against God. Examine our works the same way: if the teaching reforms the brothers off the streets and restores our people's identity worldwide, it is of the Most High; the more they persecute, lock up, and kill, the faster prophecy is filled toward the number to be sealed, so every move is checkmate.

The council agreed with Gamaliel, and when they had called the apostles and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus and let them go. The apostles departed rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name; that is the level to reach, to rejoice in the beatings, jail, and loss that come with the gospel. Daily in the temple and in every house they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ; this is the pattern, to teach every day on every platform, not once a week. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

This is Stephen at the council, addressing the audience just before he is put to death. He answers the high priest by going all the way back to the beginning: the God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran. Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, dwelt in Charran, and after his father died the Most High removed him into this land wherein they now dwell, and gave him no inheritance in it, not so much as to set his foot on, yet promised to give it to him and his seed after him when as yet he had no child. Notice how Stephen recites this history off the top of his head. Our forefathers read more than their four chapters a day. When you read, you put these things to memory, so you can recite it. A lot of us cannot recite our own history, but we can recite LeBron James and the NBA stats, football stats. These men were studious; they constantly gave attendance to studying. They called Paul mad for reading so many letters. Our forefathers were addicted to this gospel.

The Most High spoke that Abraham's seed should sojourn in a strange land and be brought into bondage and treated evil four hundred years, and the nation to whom they were in bondage he would judge, and after that they would come forth and serve him in this place. Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt, but the Most High was with him and delivered him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, who made him governor over Egypt and all his house. When the famine came over Egypt and Canaan, Jacob heard there was corn in Egypt and sent out our fathers first; the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren, and Joseph's kindred was made known to Pharaoh. Jacob went down into Egypt with threescore and fifteen souls, and he and our fathers died and were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money.

As the time of the promise drew near which the Most High had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who knew not Joseph. The same dealt subtly with our kindred and evil-treated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children to the end they might not live.

In that time Moses was born, exceeding fair, nourished up in his father's house three months, and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son. Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was mighty in words and in deeds. That corrects the doctrine that certain Christian pastors preach, that Moses stuttered and could not speak. You cannot be a stupid man and be a prince over Egypt. He was raised under Pharaoh, so he had to learn everything of Egypt, their gods, their laws, the language. He was not a stupid man, and he did not stutter.

When Moses was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel. Contrary to the movie The Ten Commandments, Moses always knew who he was; his own mother raised and nursed him, so he knew his brothers, he was only raised under the household of the Egyptians. Seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him and smote the Egyptian, supposing his brethren would understand that the Most High by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not. The next day, striving to make peace, he was thrust away with, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? Only the Most High could set a man to judge. This is the crabs in a barrel spirit: even after you help somebody, they say, Who are you to be over us? Everybody wants to be the head, the chief, a leader, but nobody wants to be a follower, and nobody wants to give credit when credit is due. The Most High was using the status Moses had in Egypt to help his brother, and they used it against him: Wilt thou kill me as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday? Certain of us will be put in different positions in this society, in politics, in education, and the Most High will use those accolades to your advantage, the same way he used Moses to go to Pharaoh and not be put to death right off the bat. Then Moses fled and was a stranger in the land of Midian, understanding that if he stayed among his own people they would get him killed, and there he begat two sons. People use the excuse that Moses married an Ethiopian to justify interracial marriage, saying maybe the Lord would forgive them the same way. But the Most High says, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy. You are not Moses. Ask Aaron and Miriam, whom the Most High plagued in the skin and put out of the camp seven days for speaking against a matter that did not concern them. Do not point fingers and compare yourself to the person next to you, wondering why one brother is judged for a matter and another is treated differently. Different judgments belong to the Most High. You are not David; do not weigh Saul's sins against David's and assume you know how the Most High will judge, the way men questioned why Uzza was struck for touching the ark. Work out your own soul salvation with fear and trembling, study to be quiet, and mind your own business.

Forty years later, Moses now eighty years old, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush at Mount Sinai. Brothers and sisters say they are too old to repent; you are never too old. The Most High used Moses at eighty to deliver the whole nation, and retained his strength. The voice of the Lord said, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses trembled and durst not behold. He was told to put off his shoes, for the place was holy ground, and the Most High said, I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, I have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them; now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

This Moses, whom they refused saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge, the same did the Most High send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared in the bush. Be careful with one another; the same person you reject is the same person the Most High raises up over you. This is the spirit of preeminence, not wanting another brother to rule over you because you believe you should be in that position. The Most High sees the heart and knows the spirits he is setting up. Moses was the meekest, most humble man. For a prince to go down to people counted as slaves and servants, defend them, and risk himself for a stiffnecked and rebellious people, shows he loved his people even in his position of authority. This is that Moses who said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren like unto me; him shall ye hear. Stephen rehearsed all the history to bring them up to Christ, because the whole ministry throughout Acts is Christ's name preached in the place of animal sacrifice. Even as Pharisees, they knew this prophecy, so he made it plain: the prophet Moses spoke about is that Christ.

This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him in Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received the lively oracles to give unto us. The one in the church in the wilderness is that Christ, the prophet of verse 37. Our fathers would not obey him but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt, telling Aaron, Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses we know not what is become of him. They did not obey Christ in the wilderness, just as they did not obey Christ in his day. They made a calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands, so the Most High gave them up to worship the host of heaven; they took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Remphan, figures they made to worship, and he carried them away beyond Babylon.

Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, made according to the fashion Moses had seen, which our fathers brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom the Most High drove out before their face. That Jesus is Joshua, and the Most High drove out the nations before the fathers. This continued unto the days of David, who found favor before the Most High and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, but Solomon built him a house. Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool; what house will ye build me, saith the Lord, or what is the place of my rest? Hath not my hand made all these things?

Stephen turns it on them: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost; as your fathers did, so do ye. The Holy Ghost the fathers resisted in the wilderness is the same Holy Ghost resisted in Christ's day, and that Holy Ghost is first and foremost the laws. There are three forms of the Holy Ghost taught in this series: first the laws, when you keep the laws of the Most High; then wisdom and understanding, which comes after you keep the laws; and then power, as the apostles received power to speak in tongues and perform miracles. Which of the prophets did their fathers not persecute? They slew them that showed before of the coming of the Just One, of whom they had now been the betrayers and murderers, who received the law by the disposition of angels and kept it not.

When they heard these things they were cut to the heart and gnashed on him with their teeth. But Stephen, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of the Most High and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city, and stoned him; the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen, calling on the Most High, said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, and kneeling down he cried, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge, and fell asleep. This is the same spirit Christ had when he said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

When the Most High cut off the nations of the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and Israel succeeded them and dwelt in their cities and houses, Israel was to separate three cities in the midst of the land and prepare the way to them. This law goes into accidental death, what the Bible sometimes calls manslaughter. An Israelite who accidentally killed another could flee to one of these three cities of refuge, where the avenger of blood could not seek him out and kill him there to revenge the blood of his nearest of kin.

Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past, means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident. The example given is two men hewing wood, and the axe head slips from the helve and strikes the neighbour that he die: he shall flee to one of those cities and live. The avenger of blood is the nearest of kin, and while his heart is hot he may pursue and overtake the slayer because the way is long. But the slayer was not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time past; there was no premeditation, no intention to kill. Accidents happen, and the Most High put laws in place for when these things happened. If it was for sure an accident, the man is not worthy of death, as the scripture says.

If the Lord enlarge thy coast as he sware unto the fathers, then three more cities were to be added. As Israel grew and possessed more of the land of Canaan, more cities of refuge were established where a slayer could flee from the avenger of blood. The purpose is stated plainly: that innocent blood be not shed in the land which the Lord giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.

This gives the distinction between an accident and intentional killing; this is describing murder. He hated his neighbour and lay in wait for him: he devised a scheme, waited for the right opportunity and the right time, rose up against him, and smote him mortally that he died. The murderer cannot then run to a city of refuge to lay low. Those cities were not established for him; they were established so retaliation did not come on those who accidentally brought harm to somebody. The elders of his own city shall fetch him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him: putting away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel is what makes it go well with the nation.

What is a landmark? It pays to use tools outside the scriptures, because what good is reading the Bible without understanding of the words written in it. The Zondervan Bible Dictionary defines a landmark as an object, stone, or post used to mark the boundary of a field, and notes that removal of landmarks was prohibited by the Mosaic law. The landmark establishes the boundaries of a man's property, where it begins and where it ends. A man who keeps nudging his neighbour's landmark over little by little until he has taken an acre is stealing land; the dictionary notes it was considered equal to theft.

One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin. One man alone saying he saw a theft is not proof; anybody can come and lie and get people put to death, imprisoned, or beaten. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. It has to be clear-cut; two or three solid witnesses, not one solid witness and a shaky witness. We deal with facts.

When a false witness rises up, both men in the controversy stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges of those days. False accusation is real: people will lie on a man to cover themselves, and false witnesses arise among your own people as well, which is part of why the nation fell into captivity. The judges shall make diligent inquisition: they get to the bottom of the matter and find out exactly who is telling the truth, who is lying, and what the facts are. A judge cannot judge a matter off what one person says; each side tells the story in his own favour, so you must examine the whole matter, question both sides against each other, and decipher the truth. Diligent inquisition is what separates a good judge from a bad judge; a lazy or partial judge makes false judgment. If the witness is found false, then shall ye do unto him as he had thought to have done unto his brother. Accuse a man falsely of stealing, and the judgment for stealing comes on you; accuse him falsely of adultery or another sin punishable by death, and you are put to death, because that is what you intended for your neighbour. So is evil put away from Israel.
The judgment is public and it teaches: those which remain shall hear and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil among you.

Thine eye shall not pity: in this time under Moses it was life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law. Christ spoke on this saying, because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge. Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean. [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.

He rides into Jerusalem on an ass and a colt, and the multitudes spread their garments and branches in the way, crying Hosanna to the son of David. All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet.

He casts out them that sold and bought in the temple and overthrows the tables of the moneychangers, saying, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.
The chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did and were sore displeased. The works themselves angered them.

The fig tree with leaves and no fruit withers away at his word, and the disciples marvel at how soon it withered. If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and it shall be done.

Asked by what authority he does these things, he asks them first whether the baptism of John was from heaven or of men. They reason among themselves and will not answer, because either answer condemns them, so he does not answer them either.

Of the two sons, the one who said I will not and afterward repented and went is the one that did the will of his father. The publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you. These were teachers of the law who were not doers of it. John came in the way of righteousness and they believed him not, and when they had seen it they repented not afterward that they might believe him.

The householder sends servants for the fruits of his vineyard and they are beaten, killed and stoned; last of all he sends his son, and the husbandmen kill him to seize the inheritance. The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner. This is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes. Therefore the kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof. The chief priests and Pharisees perceived that he spake of them. --- Topics: [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works, for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and lay them on men's shoulders, but will not move them with one of their fingers.

All their works they do for to be seen of men. They love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the markets. He that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Woe unto you: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. They devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer, and shall receive the greater damnation. There is a lesson in what they would not do. Where leadership provokes a man to works and he finds himself falling behind, he should take it to heart, because telling people who they are without putting in the labour yields no fruit.

They compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Their rules about swearing by the gold rather than the temple, and by the gift rather than the altar, are called out as blindness: the temple sanctifies the gold and the altar sanctifies the gift.

They pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin and have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

They make clean the outside of the cup and platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Cleanse first that which is within. They are likened unto whited sepulchres, beautiful outward but within full of dead men's bones. Outwardly they appear righteous unto men, but within are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

They build the tombs of the prophets and say they would not have shed their blood, and by saying it they witness against themselves that they are the children of them which killed the prophets. Upon them comes all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias. This is the plainest speaking in the gospel. Christ was no soft man with these teachers of the law who did not believe it.
O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.

verses.text: Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles.
If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.
And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all,
Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.
And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation;
And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.
Then from that day forth they took counsel together for to put him to death.
Then assembled together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,
And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.
Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death;
But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses,
And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.
And the high priest arose, and said unto him, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?
But Jesus held his peace. And the high priest answered and said unto him, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us whether thou be the Christ, the Son of God.
Jesus saith unto him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.
Do not join your hand with a wicked man to be an unrighteous witness.
You shall not testify in a dispute for the sake of following the majority and thus pervert justice.
At the testimony of two or three witnesses shall the fact of the matter be established.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
You shall keep far from a false matter.
The judge that justifies the wicked and condemns the just is an abomination to God.
Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
We are not to have hypocritical leaders because they ensnare the people.
